newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans turn up, led by Aug on thin supply.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans turn up, led by Aug on thin supply.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures turned higher in early trade, led by August which shot up on continued concerns of tight nearby supplies, traders said.

The August contract is set to expire on August 20. Although there were 35,000 bushels of soybeans posted for delivery on Friday, traders noted the open interest in the August remained high and deliverable supplies were not sufficient to cover that volume.
Preliminary CBOT data showed open interest in the August fell by 7.2 million bushels on Thursday but remained at 21.8 million, a level traders said was still too high for comfort.

Some cash soybean basis levels rose further early Friday and U.S. Gulf CIF soybean values were also higher, indications of tight nearby supplies, traders said. There was also continued talk of vessels waiting to load soybeans at the Gulf and at the Great Lakes.
At 0959 CDT, soybeans were up 16-1/2 to 1/2 cent per bushel with August up 16-1/2 cents at $7.89 a bushel.
